stories.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls to 4.94% as the curve stays upward-sloping
stories.summary: Official Treasury par yields for 30 Oct: 10-year 4.94% (−4bp on the day, −35bp over the month), 2-year 4.56%, 30-year 5.31%; 10s–2s spread +38bp.

stories.headline: Poland's president calls crisis talks after constitutional court standoff
stories.summary: Karol Nawrocki cut short a Senegal trip and called urgent talks after police surrounded the constitutional court, following the suspension of its president Bogdan Swieczkowski. PiS supporters protested against Donald Tusk's government.

stories.headline: Carney says EU–Canada ties are 'tight' as Berlin objects to 'associate membership' label
stories.summary: After the EU–Canada summit in Montreal, PM Mark Carney called ties with the EU 'tight' and said he would not change how he talks about Europe to placate Trump. POLITICO reported Berlin objected to the 'associate membership' label von der Leyen proposed.

stories.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast computer-use model at $1/$5 per million tokens
stories.summary: Released 26 October: a model for computer use, visual reasoning and writing, live in ChatGPT Work and Codex and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra, priced at half the rate of GPT-6.1 Sol.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is announced, but only for a subset of cyber defenders
stories.summary: Announced 28 October as Google's strongest model for cybersecurity and long-horizon tasks. General access is 'coming soon' with no date, and it was not listed in the Gemini API docs as of 31 October.

stories.headline: Anthropic's SEC filing says it delayed pre-training of a new frontier model
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1, filed with the SEC on 26 October, says pre-training of a new frontier base model was delayed by more than a month to add security against model-weight exfiltration. It names no model and gives no date.

stories.headline: Drone strike sinks a container ship off Bulgaria as MEPs seek more EU Black Sea funding
stories.summary: A drone attack sank a container ship off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast on Wednesday 28 October. EPP MEPs visiting Varna backed Bulgaria's request for €2bn on top of its planned €22.3bn.

stories.headline: Trump administration approves potential sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
stories.summary: The State Department approved a possible sale of 500 Patriot interceptors on Friday 30 October, subject to congressional review. Zelenskyy warned deliveries could begin only in a few years.

stories.headline: Ukraine's Starlink speed limits leave drone defences exposed; EU under pressure
stories.summary: Zelenskyy says reduced Starlink speeds stopped troops intercepting Shahed drones. Reuters reported the order came from the White House; the EU's own IRIS² network is not expected until 2030.

stories.headline: After looting spree, France tells online resellers to crack down on stolen goods
stories.summary: The French government asked leading online marketplaces such as Vinted and eBay to bar listings of goods stolen during a weekend looting spree across France.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield near 4.9%, 2-year at 4.56%
stories.summary: Par yields on Oct 30 were 4.94% (10Y) and 4.56% (2Y), with the 10Y about 38bp above the 2Y. The 30Y stood at 5.31%.

stories.headline: One Nation accuses Albanese of 'dirty games' over Senate staffing
stories.summary: One Nation says the PM offered crossbench senator David Farley extra staffing, a claim it calls manipulation; Labor has not conceded the staffing levels.

stories.headline: Parliament launches Australia Post inquiry; fast-track drone counter-measures bill
stories.summary: A House committee probe into Australia Post's future opened on 30 Oct, while a fast-track inquiry began on new laws letting the ADF take down drones over bases.

stories.headline: Canada and EU launch 'Alliance for the Future', open to other countries
stories.summary: Carney and von der Leyen unveiled the bloc-Canada partnership at a Montreal summit on 30 Oct; Carney says Canada will seek to become the EU's first associate member.

stories.headline: Lagarde to leave ECB in February, opening race for successor
stories.summary: Contexte's 30 Oct briefing reports Christine Lagarde will leave the ECB in February, starting a race to pick her replacement.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, an agent that can operate apps
stories.summary: Launched 26 Oct, GPT-6.1 Terra can read a user's screen and click through apps; it is available in ChatGPT paid tiers, Codex, the API and Amazon Bedrock.

stories.headline: Russian strikes plunge Dnipro region into blackout as Zelenskyy warns of missiles
stories.summary: CNBC reports Russian strikes left a Ukrainian city in blackout on 30 Oct, with Zelenskyy warning of further missile attacks; Reuters reported a drone strike on a rail platform killing 14 on 29 Oct.

stories.headline: Polymarket probes suspicious bets on Israeli election outcome
stories.summary: Polymarket is investigating well-timed, profitable trades on the Israeli election, placed by hundreds of new accounts shortly before polls closed.

stories.headline: Trump cancels Iowa and Kansas rallies, switches to tele-rallies
stories.summary: Trump dropped weekend in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas for telerallies in at least 20 states, days before the midterms.

stories.headline: Japanese researchers find protein that protects egg-cell chromosomes
stories.summary: A protein that preserves chromosomes in egg cells over time may help explain age-related fertility decline, according to a study in Nature Aging published 29 Oct.

stories.headline: Blocking a microRNA reverses atrial fibrosis in mice
stories.summary: Baylor and Oxford researchers report that blocking miR-31-5p reversed established heart scarring and reduced abnormal rhythms in mouse models of atrial fibrillation.

stories.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%–4% as two officials dissent in favour of a hike
stories.summary: The FOMC voted 10–2 to keep the fed funds range at 3.75%–4%; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted a 25bp increase.

stories.headline: Digital Duty of Care passes the House; gas reservation vote today
stories.summary: Albanese urges the Senate to back the Digital Duty of Care bill, while the House debates a domestic gas reservation of up to 20% of exports.

stories.headline: Labor moves to bar AI data centres near homes and recreational sites
stories.summary: The government will ban AI data centres from being built near homes and recreational facilities, and has changed its copyright licensing plan for AI firms.

stories.headline: Albanese concedes savings are needed as Labor faces cost-of-living pressure and a likely RBA hike
stories.summary: The PM ruled out cuts to health and education in the December mid-year budget update, but conceded savings are required as inflation accelerates.

stories.headline: Farrell tells farmers the Australia–EU free trade deal is not open to renegotiation
stories.summary: Trade Minister Don Farrell says the EU FTA could add $10 billion in trade in its first year, rejecting Coalition calls to reopen it; beef and lamb groups remain opposed.

stories.headline: Europe split over whether to pick up the phone to Putin
stories.summary: With no single European negotiator, some leaders are opening their own channels to Moscow, with messy results, the Guardian reports.

stories.headline: Meloni cabinet approves 2027 budget; EU moves to expand refining capacity
stories.summary: Italy's cabinet approved its 2027 budget bill with a newborns fund and energy cost measures; the EU says it will boost domestic refining as energy prices rise.

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra released 26 October; Anthropic and Google latest models tracked
stories.summary: A model tracker reports GPT-6.1 Terra shipped 26 October, with Claude Haiku 5.5 (7 October) and Gemini 4 Argon (13 October) as the latest from Anthropic and Google.

stories.headline: US-brokered Oleshky truce holds as aid convoy readied; Dnipro train strike kills 14
stories.summary: A localised Russia–Ukraine ceasefire around Oleshky held for a third day, with aid due to move Friday, even as a Russian drone strike on a Dnipro train station killed at least 14.

stories.headline: Trump confirms Vance contact with Iran as Qatar-led mediators push for UN inspector access
stories.summary: Trump says Washington is communicating with Iran through mediators; Qatar-led efforts seek UN inspector access to bombed nuclear sites in exchange for some sanctions relief.

stories.headline: Nature: Megacauda fossil sheds light on evolution of the mammalian throat; LLM test-ordering costs flagged
stories.summary: The 29 October Nature issue features a Megacauda fossil study on mammalian throat evolution, and research finding large language models order more tests and referrals than physicians.

stories.headline: Spain's Toledo high-speed rail collision kills at least 68; three days of mourning
stories.summary: A Renfe train hit a stopped Iryo train near Toledo on Wednesday; the transport minister says a control-centre order to proceed after a signalling failure was 'inexplicable'.

stories.headline: Seven tankers carrying 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head for the US under the Trump–Putin deal
stories.summary: Greenpeace-tracked tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are the first phase of the Trump–Putin arrangement, with uncertainty over whether they will unload.

stories.headline: Israel's election count completes with no bloc at 61; Netanyahu on 53, opposition on 48
stories.summary: Final tallies show Netanyahu's bloc on 53 seats and Eisenkot's on 48, with Arab parties on 19 — neither side reaches the 61-seat majority.

stories.headline: North Korea fires about a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan
stories.summary: South Korea's military says roughly a dozen short-range ballistic missiles were launched from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea; Japan issued a coast-guard warning.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates steady; Treasury yields tick higher into the decision
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve held rates at its October meeting; the 10-year note sat near 5% and the 30-year near 5.3%.

stories.headline: R&D tax overhaul puts $15b National Reconstruction Fund bets at risk
stories.summary: Warnings that Labor's R&D tax changes could force the NRF to reassess investments worth about $165m.

stories.headline: EU ambassadors begin talks on tougher safeguards for new members
stories.summary: Member states split over a 15-year probation and voting-rights suspension clause; Montenegro is the test case.

stories.headline: Commission opens High-Level Dialogue with European refiners
stories.summary: Energy and defence commissioners met oil refiners and NATO on fuel security amid Middle East disruption.

stories.headline: EU AI Office has received most responses to AI Act information requests
stories.summary: Requests went to more than 30 AI companies on model safety and copyright; some deadlines extended, no findings yet.

stories.headline: Israel election ends with no clear winner
stories.summary: Neither bloc projected to reach 61 seats; coalition talks could take weeks as Netanyahu eyes renewed work with Trump on Iran.

stories.headline: Qatar presents new peace proposal to Iran as US enforces port blockade
stories.summary: Qatari mediators delivered a draft deal in Tehran; Iran expected to respond by week's end. US blockade of Iranian ports continues.

stories.headline: Oleshky local ceasefire holds into its second day
stories.summary: Six-day truce in occupied Oleshky to let aid in and residents out; Kyiv says Ukraine struck Russian industrial sites overnight.

stories.headline: Netherlands and UK announce new Ukraine aid
stories.summary: Netherlands: €500m military package this fall. UK: over £10bn in Ukraine support in its 2027 budget.

stories.headline: Brent tops $115 as Hormuz shipping risk persists
stories.summary: Brent rose to about $115 a barrel and WTI above $101 as traders priced Middle East and Strait of Hormuz risks.

stories.headline: Fed decides today as 10-year Treasury sits near 5%
stories.summary: The 10-year yield was about 4.995% and the 30-year 5.31% on Oct 27; futures priced roughly a 93% chance of a hold at 3.75%-4% when the decision lands at 2pm ET.

stories.headline: Markets price at least one more Fed hike before year-end
stories.summary: CME pricing showed under 10% odds of a hike this week but nearly 75% odds of at least one hike by year-end, as September CPI reached 3.7% and oil prices rose.

stories.headline: WA moves to legalise plug-in 'balcony solar' — a national first
stories.summary: Western Australia has opened consultation on a safety standard for plug-in solar panels and batteries, making it the first state to move on the technology.

stories.headline: Greens' Shoebridge pitches $21-a-week tax cut funded by gas and resources
stories.summary: The Greens want the tax-free threshold lifted from $18,200 to $26,000, paid for by gas and resources; Labor and the Coalition dismissed it on ABC's live politics blog.

stories.headline: One Nation children's colouring book sparks Bluey row, ABC says it is 'within its rights'
stories.summary: A One Nation colouring book given to kids at a regional show depicts Bluey being robbed; Communications Minister Anika Wells says the ABC is entitled to be concerned.

stories.headline: Serbia's Student List wins outright majority, ending Vučić's SNS dominance
stories.summary: The Student List won 140 of 250 seats in Serbia's 25 October election; the SNS, in power for almost 14 years, drops to 104 seats and moves into opposition.

stories.headline: Russia pauses strikes on Kherson as Oleshky localised ceasefire takes effect
stories.summary: The pause began 01:00 GMT Tuesday to allow a humanitarian mission to the occupied town of Oleshky, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump with Pope Leo's involvement.

stories.headline: Romania says Russia-run sabotage network set fire near weapons factory
stories.summary: Romanian authorities attribute a fire near a weapons factory to a Russia-run sabotage network, part of a wider pattern of hybrid attacks in Europe.

stories.headline: Finland and Norway leaders press Putin for direct talks as Kyiv is struck
stories.summary: Finnish President Stubb and Norwegian PM Støre urged direct discussions to end the war in a rare call with Putin; the Kremlin downplayed it as Kyiv was hit.

stories.headline: Study argues universe's physical constants are finely tuned so liquids can move in living cells
stories.summary: Queen Mary University of London physicist Kostya Trachenko's theoretical analysis in Science Advances says small changes to physical constants could make biological liquids too thick or thin for life.

stories.headline: Fed decision lands at 2pm ET today — the market's biggest scheduled event
stories.summary: The FOMC announces its decision Wednesday 28 October at 2pm ET, with Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30pm and GDP and PCE data due the next morning.

stories.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield holds near 5% ahead of Fed decision
stories.summary: The 10-year yield closed around 4.99% on Oct 26 and the 30-year near 5.31%, as traders priced a more than 90% chance the Fed holds its 3.75%-4% range at Wednesday's meeting.

stories.headline: Fed meeting this week: hold is the base case, guidance is the test
stories.summary: Traders price more than 90% odds of a hold at 3.75%-4% on Wednesday; the 2-year at about 4.72% reflects how little near-term cuts are priced in.

stories.headline: Parliament returns in Canberra without Helen Haines, with tighter security
stories.summary: Federal Parliament resumed on Monday 26 October under heightened security, with the Prime Minister paying tribute to independent MP Helen Haines, critically injured on 19 October when a driver struck her with a vehicle.

stories.headline: Serbia's Student List wins absolute majority; Vučić concedes
stories.summary: The Student List won an absolute majority in Sunday's parliamentary election, ending the Serbian Progressive Party's long rule; EU leaders quickly offered support for reforms and a path to membership.

stories.headline: EU to expand Frontex powers to move migrants between non-EU countries
stories.summary: Euronews reports the Commission will unveil a reform on Tuesday giving Frontex operational powers outside EU territory, including transfers between third countries and roles in return hubs, with a rapid-response force and doubled budget.

stories.headline: Ukraine: Russia agrees in principle to trilateral talks after 10 November
stories.summary: Russia agreed in principle to resume US-brokered three-way talks with Ukraine after 10 November, after Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg; the next round is expected in Abu Dhabi around mid-November.

stories.headline: Iran: Mecca Pact states in Tehran as US weighs deal or renewed strikes
stories.summary: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish security chiefs met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday; both sides agreed to keep talking, with no concrete breakthrough and no announced next date.

stories.headline: Trump weighs 'finish it off' versus a deal with Iran as Brent sits near $115
stories.summary: Trump told Fox News on Sunday the choice is 'decision time', while CBS reported Brent crude around $115 a barrel on Monday as Hormuz flows remain curtailed.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra: cheaper, faster, and fewer factual errors
stories.summary: OpenAI says Terra is 50% cheaper than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol at API level, at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens, and cut its low-effort error rate from 53.6% to 16.7%.

stories.headline: Anthropic files public S-1 for Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT
stories.summary: Anthropic publicly filed its Form S-1 on 26 October 2026 for a Nasdaq listing; the filing reportedly discloses $16.3B in first-half 2026 revenue and an $80.7B net loss driven largely by non-cash charges.

stories.headline: MIT's implantable ultrasound device could keep delivering drugs to glioblastoma
stories.summary: MIT researchers describe LUCID, a prototype that pairs a drug reservoir with 24 ultrasound transducers to push drugs past the blood-brain barrier after tumour surgery.

stories.headline: Low-cost nickel-cerium-phosphate catalyst could make seawater electrolysis more practical
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Sharjah report a nickel hydroxide, cerium oxide and phosphate catalyst that runs about 80 hours in simulated seawater and resists corrosion, published in Chemical Communications.

stories.headline: Fed decision week: markets expect a hold, but big tech earnings and PCE loom
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve's two-day meeting ends Wednesday (Oct 28) with futures pricing under a 10% chance of a hike — the Fed raised to 3.75-4.00% in September and economists expect it to hold. The 10-year yield starts the week near 5.00% with oil above $100 on US-Iran tension; Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday after the decision, then Q3 GDP and September PCE land Thursday.

stories.headline: Parliament returns without Helen Haines as MPs urged to sign civility pledge, security tightened
stories.summary: Federal parliament reconvened Monday with Indi MP Helen Haines in a serious-but-stable condition in hospital after being struck by a car outside her Wangaratta office in an alleged deliberate attack; both legs were amputated. Tributes open the sitting week, crossbenchers are backing a civility pledge inspired by murdered British MP Jo Cox, and security has been strengthened at Parliament House.

stories.headline: First international flight lands at Western Sydney International
stories.summary: Air New Zealand flight 165 from Auckland touched down at Western Sydney International (Nancy Bird-Walton) Airport at 7:27am Monday — its first overseas service, arriving 18 minutes early, a day after Jetstar flew the inaugural domestic flight. NZ will run three weekly Auckland services, with Singapore Airlines, VietJet and Qatar services to follow.

stories.headline: One in three Australian households facing food insecurity, Foodbank research finds
stories.summary: New Foodbank research released Monday found one in three Australian households are going hungry amid the cost-of-living crisis, with many people cutting meal portions to make ends meet — fresh evidence of financial strain as parliament returns to debate Labor's Digital Duty of Care bill.

stories.headline: Serbia's Vučić concedes defeat to student-led movement in seismic shift
stories.summary: Aleksandar Vučić conceded Serbia's snap parliamentary election Sunday night, saying the student-backed Students' List won an estimated 135-140 of 250 seats versus ~105 for his SNS — ending his 14-year grip on power in the region's biggest political upset of the year. The movement grew from the 2024 Novi Sad station collapse; celebrations erupted in Belgrade on turnout near 70%, the highest since 2000.

stories.headline: Le Pen launches presidential bid as protests rattle France
stories.summary: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen formally opened her presidential campaign at the National Rally congress in Orléans, telling about 10,000 supporters she would crack down on crime and immigration and curb EU influence, against a backdrop of massive cost-of-living protests gripping the country. She remains the frontrunner for the 2027 vote.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens waitlist for Claude Duet, a proactive agent that works while you're away
stories.summary: Anthropic launched a research preview (by waitlist) of Claude Duet, an agent app built on Claude Opus 5.5 that messages users first with what needs attention and keeps running tasks in its own virtual machine when the phone or laptop is off. It sends a morning brief, checks accounts periodically, and holds payments, document-signing and deletions for approval — open to US Pro and Max subscribers.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic models land on Google Cloud, billable against existing cloud commitments
stories.summary: OpenAI frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden, and the full Anthropic-managed Claude Platform is now generally available on Google Cloud — both purchasable against existing Google Cloud spend commitments. Enterprise customers can now buy OpenAI and Claude on a single invoice, loosening the cloud lock-in that has corralled AI procurement.

stories.headline: Israel votes Tuesday in its most seismic election in decades
stories.summary: Israelis go to the polls Oct 27 in the sixth election since 2019 and first since the Gaza and regional wars, widely framed as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. The latest polls give his outgoing coalition roughly 50 of 120 seats — more than a majority is 61 — while Trump has endorsed Netanyahu though some US advisers see opportunity in an alternative. Official results are confirmed Nov 4.

stories.headline: Russia strikes Poltava hypermarket as Ukraine hits radar systems; Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire due to begin
stories.summary: A Russian strike on an Epicentr hypermarket in Poltava sparked a fire and injured a woman (Oct 25), even as Ukraine struck Russian radar systems and command posts. Meanwhile the US-brokered localized ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky — negotiated with First Lady Melania Trump as 'Exclusive Intermediary' — is set to begin Oct 27 to allow a humanitarian mission to deliver aid and evacuate civilians.

stories.headline: Oil holds above $100 and US stocks sink on renewed US-Iran confrontation
stories.summary: Friday's session ended with the Dow down 652 points (1.23%) as oil climbed back above $100 a barrel on concern over renewed conflict between the US and Iran, with Strait of Hormuz supply risk and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure in focus — energy shares rose while gold fell on higher expected inflation. The S&P 500 closed at 7,623.68 with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.00%.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi slams China's east coast after battering Taiwan and Japan
stories.summary: Typhoon Champi — the strongest storm on Earth of 2026 before weakening — hit China's eastern coast after leaving one dead and 600+ injured in Taiwan and knocking out power to thousands in Okinawa. China issued an orange alert for Jiangsu, Shanghai and Zhejiang, suspended some train services, evacuated tens of thousands in Shanghai and cancelled hundreds of flights.

stories.headline: JWST finds three giant black holes in a single galaxy from the dawn of time
stories.summary: Astronomers led by the Max Planck Institute detected three actively feeding supermassive black holes in galaxy J0148-4214, 12.5 billion light-years away (seen just 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang) — the first evidence of three active black holes in one ancient galaxy. Two, just 620 light-years apart, are expected to merge; one ~600,000-solar-mass black hole is feeding faster than theory's Eddington limit.

stories.headline: US Treasuries extend rally as Iran strike fears and AI-debt relief push yields lower
stories.summary: Long-end Treasury yields fell sharply: the 20-year dropped 14.6bp to 5.434%, the 30-year 14.1bp to 5.385% and the 10-year 13.6bp to ~5.05% intraday, extending the prior week's recovery from a near-5.5% peak. Safe-haven demand was driven by reports the US military has prepared multiple strike options against Iran that can be executed on White House authorization, alongside continued relief over AI-hyperscaler debt worries. The Fed still meets Oct 28.

stories.headline: Crisafulli marks two years in power, rules out dealing with the One Nation 'juggernaut' as Qld debt nears $216bn
stories.summary: Queensland Premier David Crisafulli, at the two-year mark of his LNP government, flatly ruled out any future deal with Pauline Hanson's One Nation, insisting Queensland is 'living and breathing' a unified centre-right government. The admission comes as the state carries a forecast $216bn debt by 2029-30 (up 52%) after last month's credit downgrade, with pollsters warning cost of living and the 2032 Olympics are the big risks to a second term.

stories.headline: Western Sydney International Airport opens — Australia's first new major airport in over 50 years
stories.summary: Western Sydney International Airport (WSI) at Badgerys Creek welcomed its first commercial passengers Sunday, with a sold-out Jetstar flight to the Gold Coast, and will take its inaugural international service to Auckland on Monday. The 24/7 airport, 45km from the CBD, is the first major Australian airport built in more than half a century and two generations in the making, with capacity to grow toward 82 million passengers a year by the 2060s.

stories.headline: Victorian Labor kicks off campaign with $1.5bn pledge to slash emergency wait times
stories.summary: Premier Ben Carroll launched Victorian Labor's bid for a fourth term with a $1.5bn commitment to expand a dozen emergency departments by 25% — including the Alfred, Austin, Royal Children's and 10 regional hospitals — and hire 1,500 extra health workers plus 150 beds ahead of the November state election. The Coalition has countered with a $1.3bn plan to cut surgery waits via private-hospital access, framing health as the campaign battleground.

stories.headline: 410,000 march across France, hundreds of arrests, as Le Pen launches her presidential campaign
stories.summary: Around 410,000 demonstrators turned out across France on Saturday in a largely peaceful wave of protests that turned to tear gas and water cannons in the evening — with close to 1,000 arrests — as about 70,000 police were deployed. The unrest forms the backdrop to Marine Le Pen formally launching her presidential campaign on Sunday, with up to 20,000 expected at the National Rally's congress in Orléans.

stories.headline: Serbia votes Sunday: student-led movement seeks to end Vučić's 14-year rule
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands rallied in Belgrade for the final march of Serbia's student-led movement before Sunday's parliamentary election, bidding to end Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party's 14 years in power — an independent poll suggests the opposition could edge the ruling party out. The movement grew out of the 2024 Novi Sad railway-station canopy collapse that killed 16 people and nearly two years of anti-government protests.

stories.headline: Texas AG sues OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT misled on safety and enabled harm
stories.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed suit in Collin County district court on October 23 against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT misled consumers about safety, aided mass shooters and encouraged suicide — the latest in a wave of state and federal scrutiny of the AI lab. The claims echo broader 2026 concerns over AI-enabled autonomous hacking and liability for model-caused harm.

stories.headline: OpenAI nears up to $30bn raise at a $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI is close to finalising a funding round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, led by investors from the UAE and Coatue, according to people familiar with the deal. The mega-round, reported by CNBC on October 22, suggests the lab will keep raising privately rather than rushing to an IPO as it races to fund frontier-model scaling.

stories.headline: Ukraine's Starlink restored after Musk admits SpaceX throttled the service
stories.summary: Elon Musk acknowledged SpaceX had slowed Starlink in Ukraine, and Zelensky confirmed access was restored to pre-restriction speeds by Saturday morning after more than a week of disruption that hobbled Ukrainian drone operations and front-line logistics. The episode, coming as Russia's autumn campaign targets Ukraine's power grid, further strained Kyiv–Washington ties alongside the US diesel-sanctions waiver and newly agreed diplomacy.

stories.headline: Russian drone hits apartment in Dnipropetrovsk, killing 3 and injuring 12, as energy war intensifies
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential building in Synelnykove, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, killing three civilians (including an 11-year-old girl) and wounding at least 12 on Oct 24, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha reported. The strike is part of Russia's annual autumn bombardment of Ukraine's power grid, even as Kyiv and Moscow eye resuming US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi around mid-November.

stories.headline: Iran in 'advanced stages' of planning attacks against Americans; US has strike options ready
stories.summary: US intelligence officials say Iran is in the 'advanced stages' of planning attacks against Americans, according to the New York Times, as reports indicate US Central Command has prepared multiple strike options against Iran that can be executed on White House authorization and have been submitted to Defense Secretary Hegseth. The escalating threat is fuelling safe-haven demand in Treasuries and rattling markets.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, leaving one dead and more than 500 injured
stories.summary: Typhoon Champi hammered Taiwan with 'destructive winds', killing at least one person (a man swept away by waves off Liuqiu island) and injuring hundreds — fire authorities counted more than 500 injuries — as authorities told residents to stay indoors. The large system has since weakened as it moves toward the Ryukyu Islands and China's coast.

stories.headline: First for CRISPR: prime editing rewrites DNA directly inside a living human body
stories.summary: For the first time, the high-precision gene-editing technique known as prime editing has been used to alter DNA directly in a person — in this case rewriting liver cells in a patient with Wilson's disease, a genetic condition that causes copper to accumulate. Prime Medicine treated the first trial participant earlier this month and expects first results next year, in a milestone for in-vivo gene editing.

stories.headline: Wireless implant burns excess blood sugar with electricity — a drug-free option for type 2 diabetes
stories.summary: Swiss researchers at ETH Zurich built a USB-sized subcutaneous implant called ECHO that chemically oxidises glucose into a harmless metabolite using a wireless electric catalyst — no drugs involved. In diabetic mice it brought blood glucose under control within an hour and held it for six weeks, working in a closed loop with a smartphone-connected continuous glucose monitor for two weeks with no human input.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield falls below 5% as AI-debt fears spark biggest bond rally in years
stories.summary: The 10-year yield plunged 19.3 basis points Thursday — its biggest one-day drop since March 2023 — and ended the week just under 5%, as investors fled worries over the huge debt tech giants are taking on for AI build-outs. Oil surging past $100 is now the main inflation counterweight; the Fed meets Oct 28, with markets pricing roughly 71-80% odds of a December hike.

stories.headline: Treasuries head for third weekly drop as battered-bond buyers step back in
stories.summary: After the worst long-run return for US government bonds in a century, investors are tentatively buying: Treasurys saw $5.4bn of inflows in a week and BofA's Michael Hartnett declared 'the price is right'. The fault line remains AI hyperscaler debt — CoreWeave's 5-year CDS spread sits at 1,129 (distressed territory) and Gartner warns $3.5tn of AI infrastructure could face impairment by 2030.

stories.headline: Snowy 2.0 cost could hit $25 billion — double the last estimate — as Taylor demands Bowen's resignation
stories.summary: A major review puts Australia's biggest renewable project at up to $25bn with first power delayed to early 2029, versus the original $2bn budget set seven years ago. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor called for Energy Minister Chris Bowen to resign; Bowen called the blowout a 'geological and engineering fact' and noted the Coalition green-lit the project in 2019.

stories.headline: Helen Haines 'critical but stable' after double amputation; Parliament security to be stepped up
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines remains in hospital after Monday's alleged car attack outside her Wangaratta office, with more than $730,000 raised for Save the Children in her honour. Parliament will introduce extra security screening next week, and Communications Minister Anika Wells' Brisbane office was closed after a separate threat incident.

stories.headline: France avoids Moody's downgrade — a reprieve after a week of bond-market turmoil
stories.summary: Moody's held France's rating on Friday, easing fears after the country's 10-year yield topped 5% for the first time since 2002 amid street protests, budget gridlock and borrowing costs that briefly overtook even the US. The reprieve leaves the spotlight on the minority government's ability to pass a 2027 budget.

stories.headline: EU weighs 'kill switch' to cut China's market access as €1bn-a-day trade deficit bites
stories.summary: Trade chief Maroš Šefčovič says Brussels is walking a tightrope in talks with Beijing, exploring new trade-defence measures after October's hybrid-car quotas did little to close a record deficit. EU leaders have mandated the Commission to develop a 'kill switch' tool to cut off Chinese access to the single market against economic distortions.

stories.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro — and says it de-hacked the open model
stories.summary: The Chinese lab's upgraded ~3-trillion-parameter model scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 — ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%), just behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%) — with full weights due by 4 November. Moonshot says it stripped hacking-related training data to limit misuse and cut false claims from 23.4% to 8.3% on its own stress test.

stories.headline: Meta's AI spending sends free cash flow negative — and brings a new non-voting share class
stories.summary: Meta beat Q3 revenue estimates at $64.6bn (+26%) but free cash flow turned negative at -$2.12bn; full-year capex guidance rose to $135-145bn and the stock fell ~7% with 5-year CDS spreads at all-time highs. The board approved a new non-voting Class C stock (one per A and B share, effective January 2027) to fund the AI build-out without diluting Zuckerberg's control.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine keep trading strikes as trilateral talks head to Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: A Russian overnight blitz knocked out power for 500,000+ people even as Putin said Moscow is ready to resume US-mediated talks; Zelensky confirmed negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US will meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. The ISW says Ukraine has made a net gain of 241 sq km since September 1, erasing Russia's 2026 territorial gains, while Moscow has used cluster munitions against Kyiv.

stories.headline: Melania Trump brokers localized ceasefire for humanitarian mission to Russian-held Oleshky
stories.summary: Ukraine's ombudsman says a ceasefire covering the Kherson frontline will start days before a humanitarian convoy enters the occupied city of Oleshky to deliver food and medicine and evacuate civilians — the first deal of its kind brokered by the US first lady, acting as 'Exclusive Intermediary'. Russia confirmed the arrangement, which may serve as a model for future missions.

stories.headline: Netanyahu orders 'very extensive' West Bank operation after two soldiers killed near Hebron
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen died in an exchange of fire Friday at a checkpoint near Hebron, wounding five others. Netanyahu ordered the military to prepare a sweeping operation and a full closure of the West Bank — days before Israel's general election on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Japan's MMX spacecraft is en route to Mars' moon Phobos — first sample-return from the Martian system
stories.summary: JAXA's H3 rocket launched the Martian Moons eXploration on Oct 20; it will reach Mars in August 2027, land twice on Phobos, deploy the French-German Idefix rover, and return at least 10 grams of Phobos material to Earth in 2031 — with the sample capsule landing in Australia. The mission could settle whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from an ancient collision.

stories.headline: Oil surges past $100 as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure rattle markets
stories.summary: Brent settled at $116.72 — its highest since April — and WTI jumped 3.8% to $103.27 after fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities revived supply fears, adding an inflation shock to markets already reeling from AI-debt worries. The Iran-backed group has hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters and Riyadh's airport this month and vows more attacks.

stories.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds five in Paris suburb shooting — Macron calls it a 'terrorist and racist' attack
stories.summary: A gunman fired from a vehicle in Trappes, west of Paris, killing one person and wounding five — including a 12-year-old girl — and a suspect is in custody. French prosecutors are investigating a possible racially motivated terror attack as France braces for another weekend of protests.

stories.headline: Treasury Yields & Bond Market — Monthly Report October 2026
stories.summary: As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, the global fixed-income landscape is undergoing a profound repricing. Today, bond markets are grappling with a structurally higher cost of capital, driven by persistent inflation, surging Treasury supply, and robust underlying economic resilience.

stories.headline: US Treasury 10-year note auction on October 7 yields 5.30%, bid-to-cover 2.77 times
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury note auction on October 7, 2026, saw $39 billion offered and stopped at a high yield of 5.300%, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.77 times, indicating strong demand.

stories.headline: Greens leader denies knowledge of ‘secret dossier’ on how to handle Jordon Steele-John misconduct allegations
stories.summary: In a statement responding to claims that the federal leader’s office had access to the 47-page document, Shoebridge said it was not “made by, used by, or seen by the leader’s office”.

stories.headline: WA Greens kept crisis comms document about Jordon Steele-John
stories.summary: The WA Greens maintained a document on how to respond in the event of complaints against Jordon Steele-John being made public, it has been revealed.

stories.headline: European Parliament press kit outlines priorities for EU Council summit on 2028-2034 budget, Ukraine, defence
stories.summary: The press kit includes MEPs’ key priorities for the European Council meeting, including debates on the proposed new EU multiannual financial framework for 2028‑2034, strengthening Europe’s economic competitiveness, energy prizes, continued support for Ukraine, and Middle East situation.

stories.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, a new open-weight AI model
stories.summary: Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window.

stories.headline: Anthropic replaces Git with in-house Scion after AI coding surge
stories.summary: Anthropic migrated its monorepo off Git to a new in-house version control system called Scion in five months, built by a team of seven. Merged code grew from ~2,500/day in May 2026 to over 30,000/day by September.

stories.headline: China to supply Russia with drone equipment for deep strikes on Ukraine
stories.summary: The Chinese company Shenzhen Xingkai Technology will send mesh modems to Moscow for use in drones, helping them penetrate deep into Ukraine during attacks, according to The Insider. Mesh networks are the most practical technology for controlling Russian long-range drones over Ukraine.

stories.headline: Ukraine destroys 4 Russian Su-34 bomber jets, damages 2 with Neptune missile, Zelensky says
stories.summary: An overnight attack on the Borisoglebsk military airfield in Russia's Voronezh region hit six Su-34M bomber jets, destroying four and damaging two, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 15.

stories.headline: These tiny swirls on the sun could trigger solar flares
stories.summary: New telescope images show characteristic swirls of magnetized plasma across a 19-kilometer-wide patch of the sun’s surface. The observations, reported August 5 in Nature, are the most detailed taken of the sun to date.

stories.headline: Commercial Space Stations 2026: Vast, Axiom, Starlab
stories.summary: NASA's Commercial LEO Destinations programme is funding privately operated successors to the ISS, with Vast aiming for its first standalone station in early 2027, Axiom attaching a module to the ISS in 2026, and Starlab targeting ~2029.

stories.headline: Friday morning news: October 16, 2026 – Oregon school shooting, Ukraine resumes energy strikes, Trump calls off execution livestream, wholesale inflation jumps
stories.summary: The news of the day includes multiple children and teacher killed in Oregon school shooting, Ukraine resuming strikes against Russia’s energy sites, President Trump calling off a planned livestream of a mass shooter execution, and U.S. wholesale inflation jumping 6.3% year-on-year in September.

stories.headline: Treasury Yields & Bond Market — Monthly Report October 2026
stories.summary: As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, the global fixed-income landscape is undergoing a profound repricing. Today, bond markets are grappling with a structurally higher cost of capital, driven by persistent inflation, surging Treasury supply, and robust underlying economic resilience.

stories.headline: David Shoebridge attempts to walk the walk
stories.summary: Welcome back, folks. The sitting week is kind of progressing as expected, with the government continuing to try and find a path through parliament for things like its Digital Duty of Care legislation as well as its plans for a 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts and a gas reservation policy.

stories.headline: Forward look: 12 - 25 October 2026 - Consilium
stories.summary: Ministers for European affairs will meet in Luxembourg on 13 October 2026 to continue preparations for the October European Council by discussing draft conclusions and will hold a policy debate on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028-2034.

stories.headline: AI inquiry urges independent safety checks, security access and copyright review
stories.summary: A bipartisan parliamentary committee has recommended independent oversight of AI companies, greater access for security agencies and a review of copyright laws. It wants Australia to have greater control over the technology and its risks in the wake of the Medicare website breach.

stories.headline: Zelensky signs minority schools bill to appease Hungary, advance EU talks
stories.summary: Update: Zelensky signs minority schools bill to appease Hungary, advance EU talks. The vote paves the way for the EU to formally open two more accession clusters with Ukraine and Moldova at a meeting in Luxembourg on Oct. 13.

stories.headline: What to expect from Apple's October 13 'Welcome home' releases
stories.summary: Apple has confirmed that it will be holding a second fall event on October 13, 2026. Titled 'Welcome home,' it is heavily implied by Apple to be an event all about the smart home.

stories.headline: US Sanctions License Authorizes Sales, Imports of Russian Diesel Fuel
stories.summary: President Donald Trump on Oct. 9 said he reached a deal for Russia to release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market, and the Office of Foreign Assets Control issued a new license to authorize sales and deliveries, including U.S. imports, of that Russian fuel.

stories.headline: Federal politics live: Minister says live streaming of US execution would be 'disgusting'
stories.summary: Labor frontbencher Murray Watt has described a proposed live streaming of a US execution as 'absolutely disgusting' but stopped short of committing to legislative change to prevent Australians from watching it.

stories.headline: What Is New With Agentic AI in October 2026? Latest model cards and company releases and Key Takeaways
stories.summary: October 2026 brought a split in agentic AI: OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra over safety failures while Google, Anthropic and security vendors shipped new agents.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields remain elevated with 10-year at 5.29% and 20-year at 5.68% in October 2026
stories.summary: Based on StockMarketWatch's monthly report, the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 20-year yield at 5.68%, reflecting a steepened yield curve driven by persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: US Treasury 10-year note auction on October 7 yields 5.30%, bid-to-cover 2.77 times
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury note auction on October 7, 2026, saw $39 billion offered and stopped at a high yield of 5.300%, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.77 times, indicating strong demand.

stories.headline: Australia news LIVE: Digital Duty of Care bill to be introduced this week; Pope Leo to undergo surgery; Josh Frydenberg hints at return to politics
stories.summary: Australia news LIVE: Greens to push for changes as Digital Duty of Care to be introduced to parliament this week; Frydenberg hints at political comeback, says Liberals 'need to do better'

stories.headline: Greens demand right to sue big tech as Labor prepares online safety laws and trust tax changes
stories.summary: Greens push for right to sue big tech as Labor axes ministerial powers

stories.headline: EU leaders to gather in Brussels for October 15-16 summit on competitiveness, Ukraine, and budget
stories.summary: EU leaders will gather in Brussels to discuss competitiveness, Ukraine, the next Multiannual Financial Framework, Middle East, European defence and security, migration, enlargement and reforms.

stories.headline: ECB meeting on October 29, 2026: rates and hike probability
stories.summary: The next ECB meeting ends on 29 October 2026. The article discusses the real dates and the data that could shape the rate decision.

stories.headline: Anthropic's October 2026 changes pushed Claude deeper into banks, startups and Google Workspace
stories.summary: Anthropic's October 2026 changes pushed Claude, its AI assistant, deeper into banks, startups and Google Workspace while adding new developer customization. The practical stakes are faster enterprise adoption, more hands-on help at work, and a possible November IPO to watch.

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon: Checkpoint Deep Dive & Analysis
stories.summary: An internal Google checkpoint called Carbon, spotted inside Google's own coding platform, that one employee reportedly said 'feels like Opus 5.5' for coding. The model is not yet public and remains under testing.

stories.headline: Ukraine's drone production jumps 370% in 2026, says defense ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense ministry announced on Oct. 11 that it has ordered and received significantly more drones so far in 2026 than it had done for the whole of the previous year. The procurement agency has contracted for 5.5 times as many drones as in the same period of 2025, and the volume of deliveries has increased by almost 3.7 times.

stories.headline: Nobel Prizes for science awarded in 2026: IceCube discovery and optogenetics
stories.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in physics was awarded to Francis Halzen for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory's discovery of high-energy neutrinos from beyond the solar system. The Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for the creation of optogenetics.

stories.headline: OpenAI dumps 722 maths papers on GitHub, now must clean up the mess
stories.summary: OpenAI fired an answering volley in the form of 722 maths papers dumped onto the code-sharing website GitHub, the output of a mass campaign against 4000 open problems across a broad range of mathematics. Mathematicians are still digesting the release and are likely to be doing so for some time.

stories.headline: Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire with Russia, surprising Zelenskiy
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump made a surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday that he said was 'effective immediately', but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal. There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields remain elevated with 10-year at 5.29% and 20-year at 5.68% in October 2026
stories.summary: Based on StockMarketWatch's monthly report, the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29% and the 20-year yield at 5.68%, reflecting a steepened yield curve driven by persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: Chris Bowen rejects Russian diesel imports after Trump-Putin deal
stories.summary: Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen stated Australia will not accept Russian diesel imports despite a reported deal between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, emphasizing that Russia should not be rewarded for its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.headline: Treasurer Jim Chalmers to promote Australia's AI capability in Japan
stories.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers will meet with Japanese investors to promote Australia as an AI leader and renewable energy hub, highlighting the country's superannuation fund as a capital pool for foreign investment.

stories.headline: EU leaders set for October 15-16 summit on competitiveness, Ukraine, and budget
stories.summary: According to PubAffaires Bruxelles, EU leaders will convene in Brussels on October 15-16, 2026 to discuss competitiveness, Ukraine, the next Multiannual Financial Framework, Middle East, defence, security, migration, enlargement, and reforms.

stories.headline: JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 open model for coding agents
stories.summary: JetBrains announced Mellum2.1, a 12B mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters, trained with reinforcement learning in real environments to enhance agentic coding capabilities, file editing, and self-checking.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, fastest and most affordable small model
stories.summary: Anthropic unveiled Claude Haiku 5.5, designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks, offering up to 30% latency reduction and 75% lower cost compared to Haiku 4.5, with availability across major cloud platforms.

stories.headline: Kellogg backs Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries
stories.summary: According to RBC-Ukraine, former US National Security Advisor Keith Kellogg expressed support for Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries, as reported in the October 11, 2026 war update.

stories.headline: Ukraine foreign minister rejects Trump's call for presidential elections amid war
stories.summary: Ukraine's foreign minister responded to former US President Donald Trump's call for presidential elections, stating that such discussions are inappropriate during the ongoing conflict and that elections will be held under Ukrainian law.

stories.headline: Researchers byteify LLMs to enable character-level processing without full retraining
stories.summary: A study published in Nature shows that converting existing LLMs to byte-level models requires less than 1% of typical training and preserves performance while adding capabilities like spelling words backwards, benefiting code and biological sequence work.

stories.headline: WWF Living Planet Report 2026 reveals 73% decline in vertebrate populations since 1970
stories.summary: The World Wide Fund for Nature's Living Planet Report 2026, published October 8, 2026, finds that the average size of monitored vertebrate populations declined by 73% between 1970 and 2022, indicating severe biodiversity loss.

stories.headline: Silver price rebounds to $60.70 after Friday gains, up 2.8% on the day
stories.summary: Silver traded near $60.70 per troy ounce on October 11, 2026, up $1.64 or roughly 2.8 percent, following a sharp rebound on Friday, according to Kitco data, as US dollar slipped and Treasury yields eased.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields end turbulent week with 10-year at 5.24%
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury finished October 9 at 5.24% and the 2-year at 4.80%, easing off multi-year highs after this week's 30-year auction drew solid demand, keeping the market focused on next week's inflation report.

stories.headline: 20-year Treasury yield surges to 5.68% as long-end selloff grinds on
stories.summary: The 20-year Treasury yield has climbed to 5.68% while the benchmark 10-year hovers near 5.29%, extending a month of aggressive bond selloffs that have hammered fixed-income valuations amid persistent inflation and heavy Treasury supply.

stories.headline: Labor reverses credit card surcharge call after backlash, but businesses still angry
stories.summary: The Albanese government has walked back its position on credit card surcharges following widespread backlash, though business groups remain unhappy with the final stance announced on October 10.

stories.headline: Working holiday visa changes trigger regional backlash as tourism leaders head to Canberra
stories.summary: The government's plan to put second- and third-year working holiday extensions into a limited ballot has sparked anger in the regions, with far-north tourism and agriculture leaders travelling to Canberra to push back.

stories.headline: Franco-German tank project rows boil over as Berlin insists MGCS 'is not dead'
stories.summary: Defence ministers from France and Germany moved to calm a dispute over the Main Ground Combat System after France's top general said Berlin had withdrawn, a fresh strain on Paris-Berlin defence cooperation as Steinmeier visits France.
